rationale:
Recovery week came through clean: achilles 0 every day, the physio-flagged calf/quad/back tightness resolved by Thursday and was never an achilles signal, HRV/RHR back to normal range by the weekend, ACWR stayed OPTIMAL/LOW throughout. That's the trigger the last review named for resuming something sharper than pure easy running — not the full Saturday/Wednesday spine, because Sunday brings a race (Crete 10K, or the club 4-mile if Crete falls through, still unconfirmed as of today), and neither race gets a hard session the day before it.

So this week is a bridge, not the sharpening block itself: rebuild volume, one light neuromuscular touch midweek (6x200m at ~4-mile effort, full recovery between reps) per the plan `fixtures.json` already wrote for exactly this scenario, strides Friday, and an easy shakeout Saturday regardless of which race Sunday turns out to be. The actual four-week Guy Fawkes sharpening block gets written next Sunday once this race is known and done, not guessed at today.

Sunday itself (4 Oct) is left without a fixed session_type/distance because the race is still unresolved — he expects to know by tomorrow (28th). The notes cover both scenarios; whichever it is, a same-day form entry will let the mid-week pipeline confirm the detail rather than this proposal guessing wrong.

changes.notes: Rest - normal week rhythm resuming. Recovery week complete: achilles 0 every day, the physio-flagged tightness resolved, HRV and RHR back to normal range. Clean to build back up.
Easy 8km, conversational - continuing the rebuild toward norm volume.

First bit of speed since Cheltenham, deliberately light: 3km warm-up, 6x200m at ~4-mile effort (3:38-3:40/km) with FULL recovery between reps - jog/walk until actually recovered, not a fixed short rest, so every rep is fresh rather than accumulating fatigue - 3km cool-down. ~9-10km all in. This is a neuromuscular touch, not a return to the Saturday/Wednesday quality spine - that waits for the actual sharpening block once Sunday's race outcome is known.
Easy 6km. If a leg gym session is due this week, this is the point to have already had it - keep any heavy lower-body work at least 72h clear of Sunday, whichever race it turns out to be.
Easy 5km + 4-6 strides. Legs sharp for Sunday, not tired - strides stay controlled, not a speed session.
Easy 30-35 min shakeout, conversational throughout, no strides. The day before a race - whichever one it turns out to be - stays easy regardless.

CRETE 10K OR CLUB 4-MILE - still unconfirmed as this was written; he expects to know by 28 Sep. If Crete: still just a fun race with beers on the way over, sits inside the HM recovery window - run it on feel, no taper, no pressure on the number. If the club 4-mile instead: a genuine shot at the club record (23:30-23:39) - projections sit at 23:17-23:20 blended, 23:02 off Cheltenham alone, so realistically inside 23:39 and a coin flip against 23:30 given two weeks removed from quality work. Full race protocol either way: Symbicort 20 min / salbutamol 15 min before gun. If it's the 4-mile: Puma Fast-R Nitro 3, proper 3km warm-up, target ~3:38-3:40/km, let the habit of starting controlled and finishing quicker do its thing. Confirm which race on the form when known and the plan will update same-day.
